key_insight: NbC-reinforced Cr3C2-NiCr HP-HVOF coatings can replace conventional WC-based systems, with wear performance depending more on microstructure and carbide–matrix bonding than on hardness alone.
engineering_relevance: CrNbC and FeNbC improved coating density and hardness, while NiNbC reduced deposition efficiency but delivered better abrasive wear resistance, highlighting a tunable path for severe-service wear protection.
method: HP-HVOF sprayed Cr3C2–25NiCr coatings with NbC-based additions (NiNbC, CrNbC, FeNbC)
Compared microstructure, phase evolution, hardness, and abrasive wear behavior
Used XRD plus microstructural/mechanical evaluation to link processing to performance
evidence_signal: Abstract reports dense lamellar, low-porosity coatings for CrNbC and FeNbC, XRD evidence of retained NbC with partial Cr3C2 decarburization, and hardness around 945–1003 HV0.3 for the harder coatings.
watch_item: NiNbC showed reduced deposition efficiency and thinner, more heterogeneous layers, so process optimization is needed to avoid nonuniform coatings.
paper_title: Microstructure, phase evolution, and wear behavior of NbC reinforced Cr3C2-NiCr coatings deposited by HP-HVOF
